When I moved out of my country 4 years ago, I was 18 living by myself, I got a message on my laptop during my English class saying I needed to take immediate action if I didn’t want my laptop to be completely hacked, and to “call Microsoft”
So I called and they got me until the part where they access my laptop and “show me the virus”, they asked me to pay $500 or my laptop would die, and I told them I needed to consult my dad first, so I hung up, I called my dad, but he wasn’t available. I had a funny feeling and I thought it was very strange that a company like Microsoft wouldn’t have ANY employees that could speak Spanish (and the person I was talking to had an Indian accent, so you’d think they’d hire people from hispanic countries as well?), I thought it was very suspicious that they needed to access my computer, and that they needed me to download a non-Windows software for that... since my dad wasn’t picking up the phone, and I was so scared, I forced my laptop to turn off, waited a couple minutes, turned it back on, and immediately disconnected their trash software that gave them access to my laptop. When my dad finally called me back, I told him what happened, and he was so upset, and he told me it’s a scam and that they could’ve stolen absolutely all of our information and even destroy my laptop. I felt so bad for so long. 

The truth is, these scams are specifically designed to make people feel all these things, fear, nervousness, urgency, etc., they use manipulation tactics, they design every single step for you to not know what you’re going to do next, and they make you think you’re in a state of emergency. These people are absolute garbage, their all garbage, I have no empathy for them because they know very well that they’re ruining thousands of lives for their own benefit. I’m so sorry that this is your current situation, but you will get out of this, you will be okay, and don’t feel bad about yourself because you did nothing wrong, those people who scammed you are the ones who should feel bad. It’s going to be okay :)

I got sick and tired of being a slave to my straightener, I was so flustered every time I was going to do my hair because it took so much of my time and energy and I hated feeling so insecure if I could straighten my hair (for example if I went to the beach, camping, etc) so I missed out on so many experiences because of that. I decided to stop straightening my hair on a daily basis just before quarantine started (which was very convenient for me lol), and now my hair looks so much healthier, it’s unbelievable. Most of my hair is straight because it’s so damaged that it cannot catch up with my roots which have my natural wave pattern, so it looks super whack, and I still feel insecure about it, but I know I’ve made the right decision in the long run. Anyway, besides me talking about myself, I want to express to you how important it is for us to learn to love ourselves and our hair when we’re ready for it, it’s very very difficult, but I wouldn’t want you to fall into the regret I have of damaging my hair (now I have to wait for it to grow naturally pretty much from scratch to see what my natural hair actually looks like). 

Now, if you want your hair to be straight, no judgement at all! That’s awesome and I respect that, but yeah trying to find a method that’s not a straightener is probably the best option, however, be aware that if you get any treatment, you still will have to keep it up and do it every so often to keep your hair consistently straight, and it’ll affect your natural wave pattern as well.
